# Golden answers. Format: see the `golden` test in src/main.rs.

# Plain positive answers
> www.example.com. A
NOERROR aa
ANSWER www.example.com. 300 IN A 192.0.2.10

> WWW.Example.COM. AAAA
NOERROR aa
ANSWER www.example.com. 300 IN AAAA 2001:db8::10

> example.com. NS
NOERROR aa
ANSWER example.com. 300 IN NS ns1.example.com.
ANSWER example.com. 300 IN NS ns2.example.com.

> example.com. SOA
NOERROR aa
ANSWER example.com. 3600 IN SOA ns1.example.com. hostmaster.example.com. 1 7200 900 1209600 60

> example.com. MX
NOERROR aa
ANSWER example.com. 300 IN MX 10 mail.example.com.

> example.com. CAA
NOERROR aa
ANSWER example.com. 300 IN CAA 0 issue "letsencrypt.org"

> txt.example.com. TXT
NOERROR aa
ANSWER txt.example.com. 300 IN TXT hello world

# NODATA: name exists, type doesn't. SOA TTL = min(3600, MINIMUM 60).
> mail.example.com. AAAA
NOERROR aa
AUTHORITY example.com. 60 IN SOA ns1.example.com. hostmaster.example.com. 1 7200 900 1209600 60

# NXDOMAIN
> nope.example.com. A
NXDOMAIN aa
AUTHORITY example.com. 60 IN SOA ns1.example.com. hostmaster.example.com. 1 7200 900 1209600 60

> deeper.nope.example.com. A
NXDOMAIN aa
AUTHORITY example.com. 60 IN SOA ns1.example.com. hostmaster.example.com. 1 7200 900 1209600 60

# Empty non-terminals are NODATA, not NXDOMAIN (RFC 4592 / RFC 8020)
> b.ent.example.com. A
NOERROR aa
AUTHORITY example.com. 60 IN SOA ns1.example.com. hostmaster.example.com. 1 7200 900 1209600 60

> ent.example.com. A
NOERROR aa
AUTHORITY example.com. 60 IN SOA ns1.example.com. hostmaster.example.com. 1 7200 900 1209600 60

# ...and a missing name under an ENT is NXDOMAIN
> zzz.b.ent.example.com. A
NXDOMAIN aa
AUTHORITY example.com. 60 IN SOA ns1.example.com. hostmaster.example.com. 1 7200 900 1209600 60

# CNAME chains, chased inside our zones
> alias.example.com. A
NOERROR aa
ANSWER alias.example.com. 300 IN CNAME www.example.com.
ANSWER www.example.com. 300 IN A 192.0.2.10

> chain.example.com. AAAA
NOERROR aa
ANSWER chain.example.com. 300 IN CNAME alias.example.com.
ANSWER alias.example.com. 300 IN CNAME www.example.com.
ANSWER www.example.com. 300 IN AAAA 2001:db8::10

# Asking for the CNAME itself doesn't chase
> alias.example.com. CNAME
NOERROR aa
ANSWER alias.example.com. 300 IN CNAME www.example.com.

# CNAME to a missing name: NXDOMAIN applies to the target (RFC 6604)
> dangling.example.com. A
NXDOMAIN aa
ANSWER dangling.example.com. 300 IN CNAME nothere.example.com.
AUTHORITY example.com. 60 IN SOA ns1.example.com. hostmaster.example.com. 1 7200 900 1209600 60

# CNAME leaving our zones: return the chain, the resolver follows it
> external.example.com. A
NOERROR aa
ANSWER external.example.com. 300 IN CNAME www.example.net.

# CNAME loop: stop where it repeats
> loop1.example.com. A
NOERROR aa
ANSWER loop1.example.com. 300 IN CNAME loop2.example.com.
ANSWER loop2.example.com. 300 IN CNAME loop1.example.com.

# Cross-zone chase between two zones we host
> to-www.other.test. A
NOERROR aa
ANSWER to-www.other.test. 600 IN CNAME www.example.com.
ANSWER www.example.com. 300 IN A 192.0.2.10

> to-nx.other.test. A
NXDOMAIN aa
ANSWER to-nx.other.test. 600 IN CNAME missing.example.com.
AUTHORITY example.com. 60 IN SOA ns1.example.com. hostmaster.example.com. 1 7200 900 1209600 60

# Wildcards (RFC 4592)
> anything.wild.example.com. A
NOERROR aa
ANSWER anything.wild.example.com. 300 IN A 192.0.2.99

> anything.wild.example.com. TXT
NOERROR aa
ANSWER anything.wild.example.com. 300 IN TXT wildcard

> a.b.c.wild.example.com. A
NOERROR aa
ANSWER a.b.c.wild.example.com. 300 IN A 192.0.2.99

# Wildcard exists but not for this type: NODATA
> anything.wild.example.com. MX
NOERROR aa
AUTHORITY example.com. 60 IN SOA ns1.example.com. hostmaster.example.com. 1 7200 900 1209600 60

# An existing name blocks the wildcard, even for types it lacks
> host.wild.example.com. A
NOERROR aa
ANSWER host.wild.example.com. 300 IN A 192.0.2.98

> host.wild.example.com. TXT
NOERROR aa
AUTHORITY example.com. 60 IN SOA ns1.example.com. hostmaster.example.com. 1 7200 900 1209600 60

# ...and so does a closer existing name: below host.wild, the encloser is host.wild, which has no wildcard
> x.host.wild.example.com. A
NXDOMAIN aa
AUTHORITY example.com. 60 IN SOA ns1.example.com. hostmaster.example.com. 1 7200 900 1209600 60

# Delegation: referral with in-zone glue, not authoritative
> sub.example.com. A
NOERROR
AUTHORITY sub.example.com. 300 IN NS ns1.sub.example.com.
AUTHORITY sub.example.com. 300 IN NS ns.other.net.
ADDITIONAL ns1.sub.example.com. 300 IN A 192.0.2.153

# Data below the cut is occluded: still a referral
> deep.sub.example.com. A
NOERROR
AUTHORITY sub.example.com. 300 IN NS ns1.sub.example.com.
AUTHORITY sub.example.com. 300 IN NS ns.other.net.
ADDITIONAL ns1.sub.example.com. 300 IN A 192.0.2.153

# A hosted child zone answers for itself; reloading the parent never touches it
> x.child.example.com. A
NOERROR aa
ANSWER x.child.example.com. 300 IN A 192.0.2.200

> nope.child.example.com. A
NXDOMAIN aa
AUTHORITY child.example.com. 30 IN SOA ns1.example.com. hostmaster.example.com. 1 7200 900 1209600 30

# Not our zone
> www.example.org. A
REFUSED

# Truncation: ~650 bytes (AA is kept on the truncated header) doesn't fit plain UDP (512)...
> big.example.com. TXT noedns
NOERROR aa tc

# ...fits with EDNS 1232...
> big.example.com. TXT
NOERROR aa
ANSWER big.example.com. 300 IN TXT 

# ...and the TCP retry gets it all, without EDNS
> big.example.com. TXT tcp noedns
NOERROR aa
ANSWER big.example.com. 300 IN TXT
